Haploinsufficiency of IL12RB1 disrupts the IL-12 signaling pathway, leading to susceptibility to mycobacterial infections (MONDO:0013955). Concurrently, haploinsufficiency of P4HB impairs ER protein folding and collagen synthesis, resulting in skeletal abnormalities characteristic of Cole-Carpenter syndrome 1 (MONDO:0007204). partners.mechanism_chain: JAK2 V617F (rs123456789) —DISRUPTS→ JAK2 (HGNC:6088); JAK2 (HGNC:6088) —INCREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP483); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP483) —LEADS_TO→ Erythrocytosis (HP:0001893); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP483) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytosis (HP:0001920); Erythrocytosis (HP:0001893) —LEADS_TO→ Polycythemia Vera (MONDO:0009891); Thrombocytosis (HP:0001920) —LEADS_TO→ Polycythemia Vera (MONDO:0009891); Erythrocytosis (HP:0001893) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia (MONDO:0013955). Gain-of-function mutations in JAK2 (e.g., V617F) lead to constitutive activation of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. This aberrant signaling drives the overproduction of myeloid cells, manifesting as erythrocytosis and thrombocytosis in polycythemia vera. While congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia (CAMT) is primarily associated with mutations in the MPL gene, there are rare cases linked to JAK2 mutations that disrupt thrombopoiesis, leading to thrombocytopenia and potentially contributing to erythrocytosis through complex feedback mechanisms within the JAK-STAT pathway.
